source_locator.edition_or_translation: J. M. Ashmand translation from Proclus's Greek paraphrase; 1900 W. Foulsham & Co. new edition
source_locator.section: The Influence of Position with Regard to the Sun
source_locator.short_quote: from their second station until their occultation, they produce cold

calculation_dependencies: superior-planet position relative to the Sun
normalized_rule: For a matutine superior planet from second station through occultation, classify its quality as cold-producing.
synthesis_notes: This is a position-conditioned traditional quality, not a modern astronomical measurement or natal outcome.
review_notes: The source's four superior-planet intervals are separate rules, and this interval remains within the governing matutine scope. Footnote 32's editorial discussion is not used to expand the rule to Venus or Mercury.
transmission_notes: The interval and quality are in the Ashmand/Proclus main text. The source's sequence is expressly introduced with 'when matutine'; editorial station definitions are not silently added as main-text rules.
